context.problemStatement: Show 0.4 plus 0.3 on a number line.
context.groundingProse: Start at zero, jump four tenths to 0.4, then three tenths to 0.7. Scale zero to one.
context.seedNotes: Draw both jumps on a scale marked in tenths.

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into tenths, showing a jump of 0.4 followed by a jump of 0.3, landing at 0.7.

labels.description: Begin your addition at zero on the number line.
Move forward four tenths to reach 0.4.
Move three more tenths to arrive at the final sum.

annotations.steps: I start at zero, make a first jump of four tenths to reach 0.4, and then make a second jump of three tenths to reach 0.7.
annotations.strategy: I notice that combining decimals on a number line works just like whole number addition by moving right in increments.
annotations.misconceptions: A common error is counting the tick marks instead of the spaces between them, which leads to starting the jump at the wrong tick.
annotations.connections: This connects decimal addition directly to linear measurement and the concept of combining fractional parts on a continuous scale.
